prs.title: Add custom content support to ToolError for isError responses
prs.author: hanzili
prs.cluster_pick_reason: CI is unknown for both PRs, so the deciding criteria are diff size and age. #1824 touches 4 files versus #2511's 5 files — a smaller, more focused change with less surface area for unintended side effects. #1824 also carries a lower PR number, meaning it was opened first and has had more time for community review. Its title explicitly calls out the `isError` context ("for isError responses"), matching the scope of issue #348 more precisely, while #2511's extra file suggests a broader or differently-scoped implementation. With CI equal and no confirmed test advantage for either, the smaller diff and earlier submission tip the balance to #1824.

prs.title: fix: propagate SSE stream errors to waiting requests
prs.author: heyhayes
prs.cluster_pick_reason: CI is unknown for both. #2122 touches 3 files vs. #2374's 2; the extra file likely indicates an added test, which ranks above diff size in the tiebreak order. On approach: #2374 adds logging in message_handler — errors become visible in logs but waiting callers still receive nothing, leaving the broken control flow intact. #2122 propagates the error to waiting requests, which is the correct fix for the root cause of issue #1401 (callers never receiving SSE stream errors). #2122 is also the older PR. On every criterion that can be evaluated, #2122 is equal or ahead.

prs.title: fix: consume response body on unexpected content type to prevent client hang
prs.author: vishal-vanam
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs have unknown CI. #2438 is the substantive fix — it modifies production code to consume the response body on unexpected content types, which directly resolves the client hang in #2432. #2472 is a test-only PR (1 file, `test:` prefix) that adds a regression test but contains no fix code; without #2438's change, that test would simply fail rather than close the issue. #2438 is also older (lower PR number), satisfying the age tiebreaker. #2472's regression test can be folded into #2438 before merge if desired.

prs.title: fix(stdio_client): tolerate invalid UTF-8 from child stdout
prs.author: shaun0927
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Unhandled anyio.BrokenResourceError in stdout_reader when the peer closes the transport while a message is in flight. Both PRs add BrokenResourceError to the exception handling inside stdout_reader: #2450 catches it at each read_stream_writer.send() call site (inner loop body, returns immediately); #2456 catches it in the outer except block that wraps the entire async-for loop. Because an unhandled exception from the loop body propagates to the outer except, #2456's outer handler subsumes the protection added by #2450's inner catches — merging both creates redundant guards on the same code path. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Unhandled anyio.BrokenResourceError in stdout_reader when the peer closes the transport while a message is in flight. Both PRs add BrokenResourceError to the exception handling inside stdout_reader: #2450 catches it at each read_stream_writer.send() call site (inner loop body, returns immediately); #2456 catches it in the outer except block that wraps the entire async-for loop. Because an unhandled exception from the loop body propagates to the outer except, #2456's outer handler subsumes the protection added by #2450's inner catches — merging both creates redundant guards on the same code path. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2456's outer `except (anyio.ClosedResourceError, anyio.BrokenResourceError, ConnectionResetError)` block catches BrokenResourceError regardless of whether it is raised by the stream read itself or by read_stream_writer.send() inside the loop, covering the same race condition that #2450 targets with its per-send inner try/except. In addition, #2456 includes the independent encoding_error_handler default change ('strict' → 'replace') which #2450 does not have. PR #2450 would become fully redundant once #2456 is merged.

prs.title: fix: send notifications/cancelled on request timeout and caller cancellation
prs.author: dragogargo
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both modify RequestResponder.cancel() in session.py to fix cancellation protocol compliance. PR #2493 removes the erroneous error response that cancel() was sending (and removes the server.py workaround comment that existed because of it). PR #2514 goes further by adding the spec-required notifications/cancelled notification and importing CancelledNotificationParams. They address the same root question — what cancel() should send when a request is cancelled — with #2514 being a superset. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both modify RequestResponder.cancel() in session.py to fix cancellation protocol compliance. prs.title: fix(shared): make UrlElicitationRequiredError pickle-safe (refs #2431)
prs.author: MukundaKatta
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: UrlElicitationRequiredError fails to unpickle because MCPError.__init__ sets self.args=(code, message, data) but UrlElicitationRequiredError.__init__ expects (elicitations, message=None), causing TypeError on reconstruction via the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ path. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: UrlElicitationRequiredError fails to unpickle because MCPError.__init__ sets self.args=(code, message, data) but UrlElicitationRequiredError.__init__ expects (elicitations, message=None), causing TypeError on reconstruction via the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ path. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2555 is complete and self-contained: it adds __reduce__ directly to UrlElicitationRequiredError using the canonical Python pickle protocol and includes tests that cover the round-trip. PR #2478 defines a _restore_mcp_error dispatch helper but does not wire it into __reduce__ or __reduce_ex__ anywhere in its diff, so the pickle machinery never calls it — leaving the bug unfixed in practice.

prs.title: fix: isolate streamable HTTP request errors
prs.author: he-yufeng
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Errors in the streamable HTTP POST request path (connection failures, HTTP 4xx/5xx responses, and general exceptions) are not returned to the caller as JSON-RPC error responses, causing tool calls to hang indefinitely when the server is unreachable or returns an error. (3 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Errors in the streamable HTTP POST request path (connection failures, HTTP 4xx/5xx responses, and general exceptions) are not returned to the caller as JSON-RPC error responses, causing tool calls to hang indefinitely when the server is unreachable or returns an error. (3 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2607 wraps `handle_request_async` at the task level, covering both the POST and resumption code paths and all exception types with a single try/except block. PR #1578 is narrower — it only catches connection-level errors inside `_handle_post_request` and misses the resumption path. PR #2613 handles HTTP 4xx/5xx errors explicitly by replacing `raise_for_status()` with a status-code check and includes test coverage, but its scope is limited to HTTP status errors in POST; since PR #2607's catch-all at the task level also handles those errors when `raise_for_status()` raises, #2607 provides broader protection. The tests from #2613 should be cherry-picked or ported into whichever PR is merged.

PR #1578 is narrower — it only catches connection-level errors inside `_handle_post_request` and misses the resumption path. PR #2613 handles HTTP 4xx/5xx errors explicitly by replacing `raise_for_status()` with a status-code check and includes test coverage, but its scope is limited to HTTP status errors in POST; since PR #2607's catch-all at the task level also handles those errors when `raise_for_status()` raises, #2607 provides broader protection. members.title: fix: isolate streamable HTTP request errors
members.author: he-yufeng
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Errors in the streamable HTTP POST request path (connection failures, HTTP 4xx/5xx responses, and general exceptions) are not returned to the caller as JSON-RPC error responses, causing tool calls to hang indefinitely when the server is unreachable or returns an error. (3 PRs)
members.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Errors in the streamable HTTP POST request path (connection failures, HTTP 4xx/5xx responses, and general exceptions) are not returned to the caller as JSON-RPC error responses, causing tool calls to hang indefinitely when the server is unreachable or returns an error. (3 PRs)
members.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2607 wraps `handle_request_async` at the task level, covering both the POST and resumption code paths and all exception types with a single try/except block. PR #1578 is narrower — it only catches connection-level errors inside `_handle_post_request` and misses the resumption path. PR #2613 handles HTTP 4xx/5xx errors explicitly by replacing `raise_for_status()` with a status-code check and includes test coverage, but its scope is limited to HTTP status errors in POST; since PR #2607's catch-all at the task level also handles those errors when `raise_for_status()` raises, #2607 provides broader protection. The tests from #2613 should be cherry-picked or ported into whichever PR is merged.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2456's outer `except (anyio.ClosedResourceError, anyio.BrokenResourceError, ConnectionResetError)` block catches BrokenResourceError regardless of whether it is raised by the stream read itself or by read_stream_writer.send() inside the loop, covering the same race condition that #2450 targets with its per-send inner try/except. In addition, #2456 includes the independent encoding_error_handler default change ('strict' → 'replace') which #2450 does not have. PR #2450 would become fully redundant once #2456 is merged.

members.title: fix(stdio): handle BrokenResourceError in stdout_reader race (#1960)
members.author: ddullah
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2456: Unhandled anyio.BrokenResourceError in stdout_reader when the peer closes the transport while a message is in flight. Both PRs add BrokenResourceError to the exception handling inside stdout_reader: #2450 catches it at each read_stream_writer.send() call site (inner loop body, returns immediately); #2456 catches it in the outer except block that wraps the entire async-for loop. Because an unhandled exception from the loop body propagates to the outer except, #2456's outer handler subsumes the protection added by #2450's inner catches — merging both creates redundant guards on the same code path.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2555 is complete and self-contained: it adds __reduce__ directly to UrlElicitationRequiredError using the canonical Python pickle protocol and includes tests that cover the round-trip. PR #2478 defines a _restore_mcp_error dispatch helper but does not wire it into __reduce__ or __reduce_ex__ anywhere in its diff, so the pickle machinery never calls it — leaving the bug unfixed in practice.

members.title: fix(shared): preserve MCPError payload on pickle
members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2555: UrlElicitationRequiredError fails to unpickle because MCPError.__init__ sets self.args=(code, message, data) but UrlElicitationRequiredError.__init__ expects (elicitations, message=None), causing TypeError on reconstruction via the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ path.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2514 is the more complete fix: it adds the spec-required notifications/cancelled notification (with CancelledNotificationParams) whereas #2493 only removes the incorrect error response. Keeping #2514 makes the server.py workaround in #2493 unnecessary as a side effect, so no separate cleanup PR is needed.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: Both modify RequestResponder.cancel() in session.py to fix cancellation protocol compliance. PR #2493 removes the erroneous error response that cancel() was sending (and removes the server.py workaround comment that existed because of it). PR #2514 goes further by adding the spec-required notifications/cancelled notification and importing CancelledNotificationParams. They address the same root question — what cancel() should send when a request is cancelled — with #2514 being a superset.
